subject: Simple GUI for re-using Stan models?

messages.author: b7caf0168d593233
messages.subject: Simple GUI for re-using Stan models?
parts:
Apologies if this has been addressed before, but nothing floated to the top after a variety of searches. 

I am a long time BUGS user who moved to JAGS and now slipping over to the Stan side. I have a number of rather simple problems, that once coded in Stan, I would like to make available to users who don't really care what's going on under the hood.  Has anyone investigated simple GUI's for compiled Stan modules?  


Thanks in advance for any insight into the possibility of this and perhaps pointers to examples.

Cheers,
David Robinson

[I'm very aware of the danger of letting others run with these scissors, so please no lectures.]

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple GUI for re-using Stan models?
parts:
Daniel's done a bit with D3. But nothing that's
ready to release.

Stan is set up to let you precompile and reuse models,
but what Daniel was looking at is something dynamic
that'd let you add new data points and visualize how
it affected the fit. We were inspired by the demo
Vikash Mansinghka built for the Church system.

What do you want your GUI apps to do?

We haven't got anything like a coherent spec ourselves
for a GUI model fitter, but we're interested in building
such things for stats applications for education models (IRT,
teacher value-added models, etc.).

- Bob

messages.author: b7caf0168d593233
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple GUI for re-using Stan models?
parts:
My problem isn't much more complicated.  Probably the simplest analogy for what I'd like to do is a simple workflow chart (e.g. PERT chart) where the task times are random variables. Each step in the workflow would be a different Stan model.  Input would be simple CSV files with historical data that the user can update off-line. Plots of times (and associated uncertainties) at various points along the workflow would be the major output. For the first iteration, I think the modules would be hardwired together for a particular problem. The user would interact primarily through various what-if scenarios via changes in the input files.  

---Dave

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple GUI for re-using Stan models?
parts:
I'm sorry to say we don't have anything on the GUI front yet.

The standard Bayesian approach to inference is to jointly
model and estimate all the variables --- it's the only sound
way to do inference in most cases. Breaking apart problems
and communicating through samples or estimates is usually
a last computational resort for problems that are too big
to deal with otherwise.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Simple GUI for re-using Stan models?
parts:
Greetings from sunny London

The possibility of a GUI, or more generally, recycling compiled models as their own executables, is quite interesting. As an rstan kind of guy, my way round it is just to save the R workspace and return to that, but I think the compiled models are lost when I power off the computer? However, there is something worrying about making it 'too easy' to use, old arguments we have heard 1000 times before about SPSS and goodness knows what else. So I understand if that is not a priority for any Stan developers.

But just a minute! "done a bit with D3"??? That's just intersected two big sets of my interests. I'd like to see that!

Robert

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: A function that allows you to run a stan model and it automatically checks if it's been compiled
parts:
Hi all.  We have no gui yet but in an upcoming release of rstan we will be allowing simple model reuse.  Just use the following code that was supplied to us by Sebastian Weber.  First create this function:

stan_run <- function(stanModel, ...) {
  stanModel.rda <- gsub("stan$", "rda", stanModel)
  if(!file.exists(stanModel.rda) || file.info(stanModel.rda)$mtime < file.info(stanModel)$mtime) {
    cat("Model needs compilation.\n")
    args <- modifyList(list(...), list(file=stanModel, iter=0, warmup=0, chains=0))
    stanExe <- do.call(stan, args)
    save(stanExe, file=stanModel.rda)
  } else {
    cat("Loading cached model.\n")
    load(stanModel.rda)
  }
  stan(fit=stanExe, ...)
}

Then you can run a stan model using stan_run with the file name, for example:

fit_full <- stan_run (“ep_hierarchical_logistic.stan", data=list (N=fake$N, J=fake$J, K=fake$K, jj=fake$jj, X=fake$X, y=fake$y, mu_0=mu_0, Sigma_0=Sigma_0), iter=1000, chains=4)

The first time it runs it will compile the model and save the compiled model in your working directory.  On future runs it uses the compiled version.  But it checks the date of the model file, and if you alter it, it automatically knows to recompile.  Much more convenient than having to save R workspaces.  Also it works fine when you shut down R or turn off the computer or whatever.

A
